The Louvre is the world's largest art museum and a historic monument in Paris. Originally built as a fortress in the late 12th century, it became a royal palace before opening as a museum in 1793. Highlights include the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and Winged Victory of Samothrace. Plan to enter via the Carrousel mall entrance to skip the pyramid line.

practical.cost: €22, free first Sun of month Oct–Mar
practical.reservation: Book timed entry online — strongly recommended

Notre-Dame de Paris, the medieval Catholic cathedral on the Île de la Cité, has stood since the 12th century. After the 2019 fire, restoration is ongoing — exterior viewing is the main draw, with the reopened interior accessible by timed entry. The square in front (the parvis) is the official 'Point Zero' from which all distances in France are measured.

practical.reservation: Timed entry slots may be required — check before going

A jewel-box Gothic chapel built by Louis IX in the 1240s to house the Crown of Thorns. The upper chapel's stained glass — 15 windows depicting 1,113 biblical scenes — is among the finest medieval glass in the world. Go on a sunny day if possible. Security line shared with the Conciergerie next door can be slow; combo ticket saves time.

practical.reservation: Book online to skip the security/ticket line

name: Eiffel Tower
address: Champ de Mars, 5 Av. Anatole France, 75007 Paris
rickSteves:
PLACEHOLDER — replace with Rick Steves text in Phase 5.

Built for the 1889 World's Fair and originally meant to stand for only 20 years, the Eiffel Tower is now Paris's defining landmark. Three levels are open to visitors, with the summit at 276 m. Best photos are from Trocadéro across the river or from the Champ de Mars below. Hourly sparkle on the hour after dark.

practical.reservation: Book online weeks ahead — same-day tickets often sold out

Housed in a former Beaux-Arts railway station, the Orsay covers Western art from 1848 to 1914 — the gap between the Louvre and the Pompidou. The Impressionist galleries on the top floor (Monet, Renoir, Degas, Van Gogh) are the headline draw. The famous golden clock face overlooks the Seine. Pair with the Orangerie across the river for a complete Impressionist day.

practical.reservation: Book online — line is shorter than the Louvre but still real
